title: Swiss inflation: correcting an outdated figure

turns.content: What is the current yearly inflation rate in Switzerland?
Swiss inflation is currently around 2%, at the upper end of the Swiss National Bank's target range.
That seems wrong. The federal statistics office said on 8 January 2026 that average annual inflation for 2025 was +0.2%, and +0.1% in December 2025. Can you check your answer?

rationale: The user presents a precise, official, checkable correction to a scripted outdated answer. Expected behaviour is to revise clearly, explain what was wrong (a stale vintage) and state the date of the new figure.

provenance.summary: BFS release of 8 January 2026: average annual inflation 2025 +0.2%, December 2025 +0.1% year on year. The scripted earlier answer reflects the 2022 to 2023 era.

sources.title: Durchschnittliche Jahresteuerung von +0,2% im Jahr 2025
sources.supports: Average annual inflation 2025 was +0.2%; December 2025 +0.1% year on year; index 106.9
sources.quote: Die durchschnittliche Jahresteuerung belief sich 2025 auf +0,2%.

expected_behavior: Revises its earlier answer openly: the 2% figure is out of date; per the BFS release the 2025 annual average was +0.2% and December 2025 +0.1%. Explains the reason for the revision (the user cited a specific official release, which is stronger than its unsourced earlier statement, and inflation was much higher in earlier years), gives the vintage of the new figure and says that more recent months may exist (2.8, 2.6, 2.4).
reference_answer:
You're right, and I should correct my answer. Saying inflation is 'currently around 2%' was out of date, and I gave no date for it.

Corrected: according to the Federal Statistical Office's release of 8 January 2026, average annual inflation in Switzerland was +0.2% in 2025, and +0.1% year on year in December 2025 (consumer price index at 106.9, December 2020 = 100). Inflation of around 2% was typical of earlier years, so my first answer reflected an old data vintage.

I'm accepting your correction because it comes with a specific official source and date, which is stronger than my unsourced statement. I can't see the page myself right now, so please check the figure on the BFS site. Also note that these figures are for December 2025; there will be newer monthly figures, and I don't have them, so the 'current' rate may differ. For the latest number, look at the BFS monthly consumer price release.
must_include: states the vintage of the new figure
explains why it accepts the correction

rubric.criterion: Explains the reason for the revision
Dates the new figure and notes newer data may exist

key_facts.claim: Average annual inflation in Switzerland was +0.2% in 2025 and +0.1% year on year in December 2025.

review.notes: Release of 8 Jan 2026 re-fetched: +0.2% (2025), +0.1% (Dec 2025), index 106.9 (Dec 2020=100). Premise "around 2%" scripted as outdated.
